topic: Compound microscope and plant and animal cells
key_concepts: All organisms are made of cells.
Cells are the basic units of life.
The compound microscope is used to observe cells and their organelles.
The nucleus contains DNA and controls cell activities.
Mitochondria generate ATP through cellular respiration.
Ribosomes are the sites of protein synthesis.
The cell membrane controls movement of substances in and out of the cell.
Plant cells have a cell wall while animal cells do not.
Plant cells tend to have a regular shape due to the rigid cell wall.
Centrioles help form spindle fibers during cell division.
Lysosomes contain digestive enzymes that break down waste and foreign invaders.
